    Yes, as of April 7, 2026, Iran's Supreme National Security Council confirmed acceptance of a two-week, conditional ceasefire with the United States
    . This agreement followed diplomatic efforts involving Pakistan and China, aiming to halt attacks in the region and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with reports suggesting Israel also agreed to pause its military campaign. 
    Key Details of the Ceasefire: 
    • Terms: Iran agreed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while the U.S. paused threats to target Iranian infrastructure.
    • Negotiations: The deal includes future negotiations between the U.S. and Iran, according to reports in the BBC.
    • Duration: The ceasefire is set for a temporary two-week period, according to PBS and NBC News.
    • Context: The move led to a decrease in global oil prices and a rise in stock markets. 
    Iran stated that this agreement does not signify a total termination of hostilities, as reported by PBS.
